provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Art: landscape drawing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify elements in a landscape scene.
The pupils should be able to draw a simple landscape with layers.

Introduction:
Today we will learn about drawing landscapes. We have drawn simple objects before.

Content:
A landscape shows land and sky. We draw sky first. Then we add trees. Next we draw a river. Finally we add a house. We layer these elements to make a nice picture. Like when you see the compound from far away.

Class activity:
Each pupil will draw a landscape with sky, trees, river and house.

Evaluation questions:
What is a landscape?
Which element do we draw first?
Draw a simple landscape.

Summary:
Landscapes have layers that we draw in order.

topics.title: Art: tie and dye
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tie cloth in patterns.
The pupils should be able to dye tied cloth.

Introduction:
Today we will learn tie and dye. We have seen tie and dye cloth in the market.

Content:
Tie and dye is a way to make patterns on cloth. We fold and tie cloth with bands. The tied parts stay white. We then dye the cloth in colour. When we untie, we see white patterns. Like the beautiful Ankara we see during festivals.

Class activity:
Each pupil will tie a small cloth piece with bands and dye it in bright colour.

Evaluation questions:
What is tie and dye?
What do we use to tie the cloth?
What happens when we untie the cloth?

Summary:
Tie and dye makes beautiful patterns by tying and then dyeing cloth.

topics.title: Music: notation basics
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify beat marks.
The pupils should be able to clap a rhythm pattern.

Introduction:
Today we learn about music notation. We have clapped rhythms before.

Content:
Music notation shows how music sounds. Beat marks show strong beats. Rhythm marks show short and long sounds. We read these marks like we read words. Like the sound of the kerosene stove when it is burning.

Class activity:
The teacher will show notation marks. Pupils will clap the beats and rhythms.

Evaluation questions:
What do beat marks show?
What do rhythm marks show?
Clap this rhythm pattern.

Summary:
Music notation helps us read and play music correctly.

topics.title: Art: bead work
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to thread beads on a string.
The pupils should be able to make colour patterns with beads.

Introduction:
Today we learn about bead work. We have seen beads on our mother's necklaces.

Content:
Bead work is making things with beads. We thread beads on a string. We can make patterns with colours. Like the red, white and green beads we see during celebrations. We can make bracelets or necklaces.

Class activity:
Each pupil will thread beads to make a bracelet with a colour pattern.

Evaluation questions:
What is bead work?
How do we make patterns with beads?
What can we make with beads?

Summary:
Bead work involves threading beads to make colourful patterns.

topics.title: Music: call and response songs
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify call and response songs.
The pupils should be able to sing call and response songs.

Introduction:
Today we learn about call and response songs. We have sung songs with our friends.

Content:
Call and response is when one person sings and others answer. The leader sings the call. The group sings the response. Like when we sing in the church or during cultural festivals. We take turns singing.

Class activity:
The teacher will lead call and response songs. Pupils will respond in groups.

Evaluation questions:
What is call and response?
Who sings the call?
What do we sing in response?

Summary:
Call and response songs involve taking turns between a leader and a group.

topics.title: Art: papier mache
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to create papier mache.
The pupils should be able to paint papier mache objects.

Introduction:
Today we learn papier mache. We have made things with paper before.

Content:
Papier mache is using paper paste to make shapes. We tear paper into small pieces. We mix flour and water to make paste. We layer paper on a bowl shape. When it dries, we have a hard bowl. Like the calabash we use in the village.

Class activity:
Each pupil will make a small papier mache bowl and paint it.

Evaluation questions:
What is papier mache?
What do we use to make paste?
What can we make with papier mache?

Summary:
Papier mache uses paper paste to make hard objects like bowls.

topics.title: Drama: folk story play
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act out a folk story.
The pupils should be able to use props in a play.

Introduction:
Today we learn about drama with folk stories. We have heard stories about tortoise.

Content:
Drama is acting out stories. Folk stories are old stories from our culture. We can act the tortoise story. We need props like masks and simple costumes. Like when we tell stories during moonlight tales.

Class activity:
The class will act the tortoise story with simple props and masks.

Evaluation questions:
What is drama?
What are folk stories?
What props do we need for the tortoise story?

Summary:
Drama with folk stories helps us act out traditional tales with props.

topics.title: Art: mask making
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to make a simple mask.
The pupils should be able to decorate a mask.

Introduction:
Today we learn about mask making. We have seen masks during festivals.

Content:
Masks are coverings for the face. We make masks from paper or cardboard. We cut eye holes and decorate with colours. Like the masks we see during the Eyo festival in Lagos.

Class activity:
Each pupil will make and decorate a simple festival mask.

Evaluation questions:
What is a mask?
What materials do we use for masks?
How do we decorate masks?

Summary:
Masks are face coverings that we make and decorate for festivals.

topics.title: Music: dance steps
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify local dance steps.
The pupils should be able to perform dance steps in groups.

Introduction:
Today we learn about local dance steps. We have danced during parties.

Content:
Local dance steps are traditional ways of moving. Each dance has special steps. We dance in groups to drums. Like the dance we do during weddings or naming ceremonies.

Class activity:
The teacher will teach local dance steps. Pupils will practice in groups.

Evaluation questions:
What are local dance steps?
How do we dance to drums?
Why do we dance in groups?

Summary:
Local dance steps are traditional movements we perform to music in groups.

topics.title: Revision and exhibition
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to display their art works.
The pupils should be able to perform learned songs and dances.

Introduction:
Today we revise and show our works. We have learned many things this term.

Content:
We will display all our art works. We will show landscapes, tie and dye, bead work, papier mache and masks. We will also perform our call and response songs and dance steps. Like a small exhibition in the compound.

Class activity:
The class will set up an exhibition of all art works and have a performance.

Evaluation questions:
What is your favourite art work this term?
Which song did you enjoy most?
What dance step did you like best?

Summary:
Today we show all we have learned through exhibition and performance.
